p:cNvPr.descr: PART 5: An illustration of the class I aldolase reaction. At the top right is fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, which is a pentagon with thick lines on the three bottom sides. At the left point, CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative] bonds down to H. The top point is O, and at the right point CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative] bonds down to OH. At the bottom right point, HO (inside the pentagon) bonds down to H, and at the bottom left point, H (inside the pentagon) bonds down to OH. There is a dashed line crossing the top right line. Below this are reversible arrows. To the right is a tan box: Bonding and opening of the ring. Below this is aldolase. It begins with 1(in blue)CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative], which bonds down to 2(in blue)C, which double bonds right to O and down to HO3(in blue)CH, which bonds down to H4(in blue)C, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. It also bonds down to H5(in blue)COH, which bonds down to 6(in blue)CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative].To the left of this at the top is Lys bonding right to H over N over H. The N has two red dots and a red arrow pointing to the blue 2. A red arrow also points from the double bond line to H, which bonds right to A, which bonds right. To the right of the HO3CH is B bonding right. To the left of B are two red dots. On the left side is –B with two red dots to the right. This is left and between the H4C and H5COH. To the right of all of this are reversible arrow, where H+ in blue joins the arrow pointing right. This is step 1: Active-site Lys attacks substrate carbonyl, leading to formation of tetrahedral intermediate. To the right of the arrows is a bracketed molecule that begins with C, which bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative], left to H over N+, which bonds down to H and bonds left. Below this –B with two red dots to the right has a red arrow pointing from it up to H. A red arrow also points from the bond line between H over N+ and H to the bond line between C and H over N+. C also bonds right to O, which bonds right to H (all in blue). The bond line between C and O has a red arrow from it pointing to H+ in blue. To the right are two red dots to the left of A bonding right. C also bonds down to HOCH. To the very right of this are two red dots with B to the right bonding right. HOCH also bonds down to HC, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. HC bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative]. To the right of this are reversible arrows. Another arrow jets off the arrow pointing right to H2) in blue. This is step 2: Rearrangement leads to formation of protonated Schiff base on enzyme; electron delocalization facilitates subsequent steps. To the right of the arrows are protonated Schiff base, where C bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative] and double bonds left to H over N+, which bonds left to Lys. A red arrow points from the double bond line to the N in H over N+. To the extreme right are two red dots with A to the right and A bonds right. C also bonds down to HOCH, which bonds down to HC. A red arrow points from the bond line between HOCH and HC to the bond line between C and HOCH. HC also bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. A red arrow points from the bond line between O and H back to the bond line between HC and O. To the right are two red dots to the left of B, which bonds right. An arrow points from this back to H. HC also bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative]. Just above the last HCOH and to the left is –BH. Below this is the outside frame explained in aldolase without the molecule, and is where the proton exchange with solution restores enzyme. To the right of this are reversible arrows. Above the arrow pointing left is dihydroxyacetone phosphate, where C bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative], double bonds right to O and bonds down to CH2OH (all in a pink box). A curved arrow shaped like a reversed J sits atop the arrow and points from H2O up to the pink box. To the right of the curved arrow, it states, “second product released.” This is step 5: Schiff base is hydrolyzed in reverse of Schiff base formation. To the right of the arrows is the protonated Schiff base, where C bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative], and double bonds left to H over N+, which bonds left to Lys. C also bonds down to C, which bonds right and down to H and left to HO. The outer frame to the right has two red dots with A to the right bonding right. Below that is H bonding right to B bonding right. The bottom left has --B with two red arrows to the right. To the right of this are reversible arrows. This is step 4: isomerization. To the right of the arrow is covalent enzyme-enamine intermediate, where C bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative] and left to H over N, which bonds left to Lys. Below this N are two red dots with an arrow pointing to the bond line between C and H over N. C also double bonds down to C, which bonds left and down to O over H and right and down to H. A red arrow points from the double bonds line down to –B which bonds right to H. On the outside right is A bonding right with two red dots to the left. Below that H bond right to B, which bonds right.
